pr_title: kv: acquire clock reading for lease request under lock
pr_body:
Fixes #134171.

This commit adds validation that lease construction that the min lease proposed timestamp is never in advance of the current time.

The commit then fixes a case where this could occur by acquiring a clock reading under the replica mutex in redirectOnOrAcquireLeaseForRequest.

While I was never able to reproduce the issue in `TestRequestsOnLaggingReplica`, I did independently and reliably hit the same issue when adding lease type changes to `kvnemesis` (#125260, PR to follow soon) and confirmed that this change fixes the issue.

Epic: None

comments:
Following the investigation below, I'm removing the release-blocker label. I wasn't able to root cause this failure and it seems to be the first of its kind[^1]. At the same time, it didn't reproduce[^repro]. I assume new assertions[^ass] that were added as part of leader leases work are catching some pre-existing condition

[^1]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/57932 is the only other relevant thread that has this test, but the failure mode there is very different.
[^repro]: gceworker `./dev test --count 10000 --stress ./pkg/kv/kvserver --filter TestRequestsOnLaggingReplica -- --jobs 100 --local_resources=cpu=100  --local_resources=memory=HOST_RAM 2>&1 | tee stress.log`
[^ass]: 06d666ee715695459e77af1dc3118be90c1986f7

----

We fail here

[/pkg/kv/kvserver/client_raft_test.go#L1293-L1298](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6bb6dc96ebf0ee2f23c5c568fa0d421019dc0946/pkg/kv/kvserver/client_raft_test.go#L1293-L1298)
```go
		for {
			getRequest := getArgs(key)
			_, pErr := kv.SendWrapped(timeoutCtx, partitionedStoreSender, getRequest)
			require.Error(t, pErr.GoError(), "unexpected success")
			nlhe := &kvpb.NotLeaseHolderError{}
			require.ErrorAs(t, pErr.GetDetail(), &nlhe, "%v", pErr)
```

where the error originates here:

[/pkg/kv/kvserver/leases/build.go#L698-L700](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6bb6dc96ebf0ee2f23c5c568fa0d421019dc0946/pkg/kv/kvserver/leases/build.go#L698-L700)
```go
	if i.Now.Less(nextLease.Start) {
		return errors.AssertionFailedf("lease cannot start after now")
	}
```

In other words, we set a Get, it attempts to acquire the lease, but the `status.Now` we pick here

[/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_range_lease.go#L354-L364](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6bb6dc96ebf0ee2f23c5c568fa0d421019dc0946/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_range_lease.go#L354-L364)
```go
		Now:                   status.Now,
		MinLeaseProposedTS:    p.repl.mu.minLeaseProposedTS,
		RaftStatus:            raftStatus,
		RaftFirstIndex:        p.repl.raftFirstIndexRLocked(),
		PrevLease:             status.Lease,
		PrevLeaseNodeLiveness: status.Liveness,
		PrevLeaseExpired:      status.IsExpired(),
		NextLeaseHolder:       nextLeaseHolder,
		BypassSafetyChecks:    bypassSafetyChecks,
	}
	out, err := leases.VerifyAndBuild(ctx, st, nl, in)
```

is not compatible with the lease start we pick here (and in the rest of that code).

[/pkg/kv/kvserver/leases/build.go#L423-L433](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6bb6dc96ebf0ee2f23c5c568fa0d421019dc0946/pkg/kv/kvserver/leases/build.go#L423-L433)
```go
func leaseStart(i BuildInput) hlc.ClockTimestamp {
	if i.Transfer() {
		// For lease transfers, we initially set the lease start time to now.
		// However, this will be adjusted during request evaluation to a clock
		// reading captured after the previous lease has been revoked (RevokeLease).
		return i.Now
	}

	start := i.Now
	if i.PrevLease.Replica.StoreID == 0 || i.Extension() {
		start.Backward(i.PrevLease.Start)
```

Note that we start out with `status.Now` in both cases (since `i.Now` is `status.Now`). The only way the start timestamp can move ahead is

[/pkg/kv/kvserver/leases/build.go#L455-L457](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6bb6dc96ebf0ee2f23c5c568fa0d421019dc0946/pkg/kv/kvserver/leases/build.go#L455-L457)
```go
		if i.Extension() {
			start.Forward(i.MinLeaseProposedTS)
		}
```

so this is likely what happened: the replica's MinLeaseProposedTS got bumped ahead of `status.Now` somehow. `minLeaseProposedTS` isn't ever set to a future time as far as I can tell. I checked whether `status` maybe got initialized in an earlier disjoint `r.mu` critical section which would allow them to drift

[/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_range_lease.go#L354-L355](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6bb6dc96ebf0ee2f23c5c568fa0d421019dc0946/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_range_lease.go#L354-L355)
```go
		Now:                   status.Now,
		MinLeaseProposedTS:    p.repl.mu.minLeaseProposedTS,
```

but as far as I can tell `r.mu` is held exclusively throughout. Long story short, without resorting to explanations such as bitflips etc, I don't know how this could happen.

> Long story short, without resorting to explanations such as bitflips etc, I don't know how this could happen.

+1.

Separately, I'm quite surprised that `minLeaseProposedTS` can ever get bumped ahead of `Status.Now` in the first place. It's set when a replica is initialized (not the case here), copied over on a split (shouldn't matter as it isn't forwarded), and set when the lease is revoked:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/c22dc1355880fad0effcab554344605f21142f17/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_range_lease.go#L1027-L1036

Leases are revoked either on lease transfer or when promoting from epoch based leases to leader leases (and vice-versa). I don't see how either of these hold.

review_comments:
so what was the (or at least a possible) sequence of events here?

1. we grab `now` above
2. someone bumps the minLeaseProposedTS. Is this someone someone else calling `redirectOnOrAcquireLeaseForRequest` and racing ahead of us, which (during eval) hits `RevokeLease`[^1]?
3. but then we would join the ongoing request already, no? And that would prevent us from calling `VerifyAndBuild`, so we wouldn't error out?

[^1]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/90d1c8caa24033e6a2f77c768dab0378fa31f514/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_range_lease.go#L1030-L1036

> Is this someone someone else calling redirectOnOrAcquireLeaseForRequest and racing ahead of us, which (during eval) hits RevokeLease[1](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/135042#user-content-fn-1-53155447d858ae7b5fdcf644d14e8687)?

Yes, I added some additional logging to kvnemesis and confirmed that it is.

> but then we would join the ongoing request already, no? And that would prevent us from calling VerifyAndBuild, so we wouldn't error out?

It looks like the ongoing request completes (unsuccessfully) before the next request acquires the replica mutex. `request lease: err=[NotLeaseHolderError] ‹refusing to acquire lease on follower›`. So there's nothing for it to join to.

This timeline is strange, but there's nothing wrong with it besides the fact that we are using a stale clock timestamp for `now`, which this commit fixes.
